instanceExperimental.title: Experimental
instanceExperimental.description: Opt into features that are still being evaluated before they become default behavior.
instanceExperimental.warningTitle: Experimental features may break at any time.
instanceExperimental.warningBody: These features are opt-in and come with no compatibility guarantees. They may change, break, or be removed without notice. Avoid relying on them for critical or production workflows.
instanceExperimental.featuresSubheading: Optional product features that are still being evaluated.
instanceExperimental.developerSubheading: Internal tools for developing, testing, and debugging Kujira AI Workforce.
instanceExperimental.legacySubheading: These features are going to be removed.
instanceExperimental.combinedInboxTasksDescription: Fold Inbox into Tasks. One Tasks row carries the unread badge, and a Views menu reaches every inbox view (Mine, Unread, Blocked, Recent, Everything) and every task view.
instanceExperimental.combinedInboxTasksFootnote: Old Inbox links redirect to the matching view. Turning this off restores the separate Inbox; no data changes.
instanceExperimental.firstTaskPlanProposal: First task: propose with a plan document
instanceExperimental.firstTaskPlanProposalDescription: When the user's first request is a single task, the chief of staff writes a short plan document and a checkbox card instead of a one-card confirmation. Applies to organizations created after the toggle is flipped.
instanceExperimental.streamlinedUiDescription: Use the simplified main sidebar, shared Tasks and Inbox presentation, focused task detail layout, and contextual navigation across Agents, Routines, Skills, and Settings.
instanceExperimental.streamlinedUiFootnote: Turning this off restores the legacy shell and navigation. Task and page data are unchanged.
instanceExperimental.summariesDescription: Show Summarizer-generated status slots on project and workspace pages, with on-demand refresh and revision history. Existing summary data is kept when this is disabled.
instanceExperimental.summariesFootnote: Status Cards requires Summaries. Disabling Summaries also disables Status Cards.
instanceExperimental.isolatedWorkspacesByDefaultDescription: Treat a project that has no execution workspace policy of its own as if it selected isolated workspaces, so its tasks get a per-task worktree instead of sharing the project checkout. A project that carries its own policy keeps it.
instanceExperimental.autoRestartDevServerWhenIdleDescription: In `pnpm dev:once`, wait for all queued and running local agent runs to finish, then restart the server automatically when backend changes or migrations make the current boot stale.
instanceExperimental.managedEnvironmentOnlyDescription: Hide the local environment and run all agents in the platform-managed environment.
instanceExperimental.paperclipDeveloperModeDescription: Show internal Kujira AI Workforce maintainer tools and observability links, including Honeycomb trace queries on run pages.
instanceExperimental.serverInfoDebugViewDescription: Show a "Server" section in the account drawer with the current server restart time and running commit.
instanceExperimental.smokeLabDescription: Add a "Smoke Lab" tab under Apps → Developer and an "Integration smoke" card on the dashboard for exercising every integration path against deterministic local fixtures (fake OAuth provider + loopback MCP servers). Private (non-public) deployments only.
instanceExperimental.issuePlanDecompositionsDescription: Show accepted-plan decomposition history on task detail pages. Intended for debugging and validating subtask creation behavior while the presentation is still being refined.
instanceExperimental.classicTaskInterfaceDescription: Restores the previous task detail page: the page-level header with inline description editing, the plain comment thread, and the fixed Properties sidebar. Chat-only features — streaming activity folding, inline plan and question cards, the three-mode composer — are unavailable in the classic view.
instanceExperimental.classicTaskInterfaceFootnote: Switching takes effect immediately. No task data is affected.
instanceExperimental.goalsSidebarLinkDescription: Restore the Goals item in the main sidebar while the goals surface is being evaluated.
instanceExperimental.worktreeRunDescription: This is an isolated git-worktree preview instance. Turn this on to let the scheduler execute runs here. Only tasks created after enabling will run automatically — copied/pre-existing tasks stay parked. Toggling off and on resets the cutoff.
instanceExperimental.worktreeRunSuppressedMismatch: This setting was armed in a different instance and copied here, so no tasks run automatically.
instanceExperimental.worktreeRunSuppressedMissing: This setting is missing its activation cutoff, so no tasks run automatically.
instanceExperimental.worktreeRunSuppressedHint: Toggle it off and back on to arm execution for tasks created here.
instanceExperimental.agentChatDescription: Talk to each agent in one ongoing conversation. Clarify goals and create tasks for execution. Chat leads the Work group and opens an agent rail beside the nav, and each chat's side panel shows the agent's tasks and artifacts as cards.
instanceExperimental.agentChatFootnote: Turning this off preserves conversations and lets active runs finish, but prevents new messages.
instanceExperimental.betaSkillsDescription: Allow agents to pin beta releases of the Kujira AI Workforce core skill. Disabling this returns every agent to the default live skill without removing saved pins.
instanceExperimental.builtInAgentsDescription: Show Kujira AI Workforce-managed built-in agent surfaces, including built-in roster badges, the Built-in agents tab, and built-in agent setup controls.
instanceExperimental.casesDescription: Durable work products (blog posts, tweet storms…) that tasks create and iterate on. Adds the Cases tab and the agent case API.
instanceExperimental.casesFootnote: Turning Cases off hides the tab and blocks the case API; existing case data is kept.
instanceExperimental.chatConnectorsDescription: Connect agents to Slack, GitHub, Discord, Microsoft Teams, and Telegram conversations.
instanceExperimental.chatConnectorsFootnote: Turning this off hides experimental chat setup and connected-task controls. Existing chat connections keep running. AgentMail, GitHub tools, and other tool connectors stay available.
instanceExperimental.conferenceRoomChatDescription: Adds a Conference Room — one chat where you and your whole team work together — plus the live activity feed and the redesigned onboarding. Also restyles task threads as chat bubbles. Turn off anytime to restore the classic UI.
instanceExperimental.decisionsDescription: Show the Decisions item in the main sidebar — the attention home that surfaces the tasks awaiting your input — while the surface is still being evaluated.
instanceExperimental.enableEnvironmentsDescription: Show environment management in company settings and allow project and agent environment assignment controls.
instanceExperimental.enableExternalObjectsDescription: Detect external URLs in issues and show resolved status for pull requests, tickets, and other referenced work objects.
instanceExperimental.enableIsolatedWorkspacesDescription: Show execution workspace controls in project configuration and allow isolated workspace behavior for new and existing task runs.
instanceExperimental.experimentalFileViewerDescription: Show task detail controls for browsing and previewing workspace files relative to a task.
instanceExperimental.memoryConnectorsDescription: Connect Mem0, Zep, Supermemory, Cognee, and Honcho for long-term memory and context.
instanceExperimental.memoryConnectorsFootnote: Turning this off hides setup for these connectors. Existing connections keep running.
instanceExperimental.paperclipRunnerDescription: Allow new Codex agents to select the experimental Rust Kujira AI Workforce Runner, including authenticated runner ingress when a sandbox requires it. Onboarding continues to use legacy adapters. Turning this off hides the choice without affecting existing native runs.
instanceExperimental.simplifiedEnglishDescription: Instruct agents to write user interactions (plan confirmations, questions, suggested tasks, checkbox prompts) in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, with brief context on what information the decision needs and what happens for each choice.
instanceExperimental.statusCardsDescription: Enable the experimental shared status-card board and its gated API. Existing card data is kept when this is disabled.
instanceExperimental.statusCardsFootnote: Enabling Status Cards also enables Summaries.

governance.body: You operate as the board of directors. Agents can't hire without your approval. Pause, reassign, or terminate any agent at any time. Autonomy is a privilege you grant, not a default.

different.q: How is Kujira AI Workforce different from agents like OpenClaw or Claude Code?
different.a: Kujira AI Workforce uses those agents. It orchestrates them into a team — with org charts, budgets, goals, governance, and accountability.

existing.q: Can I use my existing agents?
existing.a: Yes. Kujira AI Workforce is unopinionated about agent runtimes. Claude Code sessions, OpenClaw bots, Python scripts, shell commands, HTTP webhooks — anything that can receive a heartbeat. Adapters connect to whatever execution environment you use.

budget.q: What happens when an agent hits its budget limit?
budget.a: At 100% budget utilization the agent auto-pauses and new tasks are blocked. You get a soft warning at 80%. As the board, you can override the limit at any time and resume the agent.

control.q: How do I keep agents from doing things I don't want?
control.a: Governance modules gate what agents can change in the control plane — for example, hiring new agents requires board approval by default. Your agents remain yours to secure however you choose.

continuous.a: By default, agents run on scheduled heartbeats and notifications such as task assignment or @-mentions. You can also hook a continuous agent into the harness.

vsTickets.q: Why not just point my agent at Asana or Trello?
vsTickets.a: Agent orchestration needs checkout coordination, session continuity, cost monitoring, and governance. Kujira AI Workforce does that for you.

setup.q: What does a typical setup look like?
setup.a: Sign in to this instance, create an organization, configure projects and agents, set tasks, and let heartbeats carry the work. Local and remote deployments are supported.

multiCompany.a: Yes. A single deployment can run many companies with complete data isolation — useful for separate ventures or parallel strategy tests.

opensource.a: Yes. MIT licensed and self-hosted. Interactive setup walks you through configuration and your first agent team.
